prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of commitments and plans

Economy and public finances
- Support the fragile recovery, then more than halve the deficit by 2014 via growth, targeted tax rises, efficiency savings, lower‑priority cuts, and asset sales. Cap public‑sector pay at 1% for two years; reform pensions; keep VAT exemptions on essentials; no rises in basic or higher income tax rates.
- Bank reform: higher capital, living wills, pay restraint where risky, competition measures, and a push for a global levy. Maintain lending targets.
- Industrial strategy: UK Finance for Growth (£4bn), Growth Capital and Innovation funds, R&D tax credits, capital allowances, and a “patent box.” Back advanced manufacturing, digital, life sciences, and low‑carbon sectors; one million skilled jobs by 2015.

Infrastructure and business
- High Speed Rail linking major cities; electrification; Crossrail; motorway hard‑shoulder running. Conditional third runway at Heathrow; 100,000 EV charging points.
- Broadband: universal basic access by 2012; superfast rollout funded partly by a fixed‑line levy.
- Green Investment Bank to finance low‑carbon infrastructure.

Jobs, welfare, and housing
- Youth guarantee at six months; mandatory work offers at two years; strengthen work capability assessments. Minimum Wage to at least track average earnings; “Better Off in Work” £40/week floor.
- Stamp duty holiday for first‑time buyers under £250k (two years); 5% rate on £1m+ homes. Expand affordable and council housing; stronger mortgage regulation; landlord register; aim to end rough sleeping by 2012.

Consumers and finance
- People’s Bank via Post Office; universal basic bank account right; clamp down on high‑cost credit; single consumer‑finance regulator; portable bank account/ISA numbers.

Education and skills
- Protect frontline spend on Sure Start, childcare, schools, and 16–19. Expand free nursery places; one‑to‑one tuition guarantees; parent trigger for leadership change in weak schools; more accredited school groups. Raise participation to 18; expand advanced apprenticeships; widen HE access; HE funding review.

NHS and care
- Protect NHS spending; up to £20bn efficiency reinvested in care. Patient guarantees: 18‑week treatment or funded alternative; faster cancer pathways; mid‑life health checks; extended GP access; wider home‑based care; more psychological therapy. Create a National Care Service: free home care for highest needs from 2011; cap residential care costs after two years from 2014; long‑term funding commission.

Policing, justice, and immigration
- Maintain police/PCSO numbers; 80% neighbourhood time on the beat; performance “report cards”; interventions for high‑harm families. Faster anti‑social behaviour action with right to injunctions; expand Community Payback. Use CCTV and DNA with safeguards; voluntary ID cards for citizens. Points‑based immigration; no unskilled migration from outside the EU; stricter English requirements; tougher on illegality; citizenship earned.

Culture, sport, and media
- Deliver 2012 Olympics legacy; more school sport and coaching; supporter trusts enabled to buy club stakes. Museums’ operational independence; more lottery funds post‑2012; protect post offices and pubs. Uphold BBC independence; complete digital switchover; update IP and curb online piracy.

Environment and rural
- About 40% low‑carbon electricity by 2020; 400,000 green jobs by 2015; renewables, nuclear, and CCS; ban new unabated coal. Smart meters by 2020; “pay‑as‑you‑save” home retrofits; warmer homes standard; toward “zero waste” with landfill bans on recyclable/biodegradable waste. Maintain Green Belt; expand woodlands; coastal access; supermarket ombudsman; universal rural broadband.

Constitution and governance
- Referendums on Alternative Vote and a democratic second chamber; fixed‑term parliaments; lobbyist register; limits on MPs’ outside roles; recall for serious misconduct. More open data; stronger local government powers; city‑region devolution; low council tax rises; finance review.

Global and defence
- Afghanistan strategy focused on protecting people, training local forces, and phased handover; improved equipment and veteran support. Strategic Defence Review; retain independent nuclear deterrent while pursuing multilateral disarmament. Active EU role; meet 0.7% aid by 2013 in law; push on MDGs, arms‑trade treaty, non‑proliferation, and UN/IFIs/NATO reform.
